name: Graphs and Dynamic Programming
description: Search graphs, find shortest paths, and solve hard problems by remembering subproblems.

lessonNames.l9-arbitrage-cycle: Currency arbitrage as a negative cycle
lessonNames.l17-dice-stopping: When to stop: a dice game

lessonObjectives.l1-nodes-and-edges: Store a graph as an adjacency list and as a matrix.
lessonObjectives.l2-level-by-level: Implement breadth-first search with a queue.
lessonObjectives.l3-going-deep: Implement depth-first search recursively and with a stack.
lessonObjectives.l4-islands: Treat a grid as a graph to count islands.
lessonObjectives.l5-tasks-in-order: Order tasks with dependencies by topological sort.
lessonObjectives.l6-fewest-steps: Find shortest paths in an unweighted graph with breadth-first search.
lessonObjectives.l7-dijkstra: Implement Dijkstra’s algorithm with a heap.
lessonObjectives.l8-groups: Use union-find to merge and query components.
lessonObjectives.l9-arbitrage-cycle: Detect a currency arbitrage with logarithms and Bellman-Ford.
lessonObjectives.l10-every-subset: Generate subsets and permutations by backtracking.
lessonObjectives.l11-dead-ends: Prune a backtracking search to make it fast enough.
lessonObjectives.l12-remembering: Speed up a recursion with memoisation.
lessonObjectives.l13-climbing-stairs: Write a recurrence and fill a table from the bottom up.
lessonObjectives.l14-knapsack: Solve the 0/1 knapsack problem with a table.
lessonObjectives.l16-grid-paths: Count and optimise paths through a grid with obstacles.
lessonObjectives.l17-dice-stopping: Value a stopping game by backward induction.
